findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving it a public IP and exposing the MySQL endpoint to the internet rather than keeping it private to the VPC. Combined with a well-known 'admin' master user it greatly enlarges the attack surface.
storage_encrypted = false means the database volume and its snapshots are stored unencrypted, so anyone obtaining the underlying storage or a snapshot can read all data.

The master password is passed directly via var.password (and reused in the EC2 user_data), so it lands in Terraform state and instance metadata in plaintext instead of being sourced from Secrets Manager or manage_master_user_password.
The master username is the predictable default 'admin', which aids credential-guessing/brute-force attacks against the publicly reachable endpoint.

The database username and password are interpolated into EC2 user_data, which is readable by any process or attacker that can reach the instance metadata service (http://169.254.169.254/latest/user-data) and is stored unencrypted in the instance configuration and Terraform state.

No metadata_options block enforcing http_tokens = "required" is set, so IMDSv1 remains available; an SSRF in the PHP app could be used to steal the instance profile credentials that carry s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* permissions.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the instance's root volume (which contains the plaintext dbinfo.inc credentials file) may be stored unencrypted.

The instance role grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*", allowing a compromised web server to read or destroy any bucket, launch/terminate instances, and modify or snapshot any database in the account.
The database security group allows all protocols and ports outbound to 0.0.0.0/0, enabling unrestricted data exfiltration or command-and-control traffic from a compromised database host.

The MySQL parameter group does not set require_secure_transport = 1, so clients may connect to the (publicly accessible) database over unencrypted connections, exposing credentials and data in transit.

The DB security group permits port 3306 from the entire VPC CIDR rather than only the application security group; since the instance is also publicly_accessible, reachability is broader than necessary for least privilege.
